question: What is the primary focus of observation as a data collection method?

options.A: Recording behaviors and events as they naturally occur
options.B: Asking participants to fill out a detailed questionnaire
options.C: Conducting formal interviews with patient family members
options.D: Reviewing past medical records in the hospital archive

explanation: Observation involves watching and recording real-time actions and conditions without necessarily asking questions or altering the environment. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h1)

question: Why is observation often more reliable than interviews in research?

options.A: It allows researchers to control what the participants say
options.B: It takes much less time and fewer resources to complete
options.C: It captures actual behavior rather than just reported behavior
options.D: It is completely free of any human bias or error

explanation: People sometimes misremember or forget details in interviews, but direct observation lets you see what is truly happening in real time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h1)

question: What type of observation happens when a researcher joins a group to experience their daily routine firsthand?
explanation: You got it! In 'participant observation', the researcher actively joins the community to get an inside perspective. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h2)

question: A nurse sits quietly in the corner of a pediatric playroom to watch children interact without joining in or altering the setting. What kind of observation is this?
explanation: Remaining detached and watching without direct interaction defines non-participant observation. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h2)

question: Which observational tool is best used to grade the quality or frequency of a specific behavior?
explanation: Think of a rating scale as a grading tool. It lets you measure the degree or quality of an action, rather than just noting if it happened or not. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h3)

question: A nursing researcher wants to mark down the exact presence or absence of hand hygiene steps among ward staff during a shift. Which tool should they use?
explanation: Checklists are ideal for recording whether specific, distinct actions occurred or did not occur. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h3)

question: In research, what do we call the 'Hawthorne effect'?

options.A: Patients refusing to give consent for data collection in the ward
options.B: Data getting lost because field notes were not written down promptly
options.C: The researcher missing key events due to fatigue during a long shift
options.D: People changing their behavior because they know they are being watched

explanation: Spot on! The Hawthorne effect happens naturally because humans tend to act differently when they realize someone is watching them. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of using observation instead of questionnaires?

options.A: It guarantees that participants will never experience anxiety
options.B: It is completely immune to any form of human judgment error
options.C: It records actual behavior rather than self-reported claims
options.D: It requires zero preparation or specialized recording tools

explanation: Exactly! People might say one thing in a questionnaire, but observation lets you see what they actually do in practice. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h4)

question: What term describes two different observers getting similar results when watching the same event?
explanation: Well done! 'Inter-rater reliability' simply means different observers agree and are consistent in how they score what they see. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h5)

question: Why is ethical clearance and consent so important even in observational nursing studies?

options.A: To protect patient privacy and respect autonomy
options.B: To eliminate all possibilities of observer bias completely
options.C: To ensure the hospital receives more funding for research
options.D: To prevent the researcher from getting tired during shifts

explanation: Spot on! Even when we are just watching, we must always respect patients' privacy rights and personal autonomy. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h5)
